newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 2.

text.p: Retailers reported stronger sales over Thanksgiving than had been expected, the Wall Street Journal reported.

- Volkswagen AG accepted the resignation of purchasing chief Jose Ignacio Lopez, removing a major obstacle to the auto maker's effort to resolve a dispute with General Motors over alleged corporate espionage.
- The National Labor Relations Board is poised to make it easier for temporary workers to join unions.
- Disney's "101 Dalmatians" had more than $46 million in box office receipts over Thanksgiving, a record for the five-day holiday weekend.
- Companies are increasingly using an arcane accounting strategy to write off certain acquisition costs rather than reporting lower earnings for years by amortizing goodwill.
- Trust-preferred stock attracted as much as $10 billion from institutional investors since its introduction two weeks ago. Sony Pictures named Amy Pascal president of its Columbia Pictures unit.
- Consumers' incomes were flat in October but that did not keep them from increasing spending by 0.5 percent.
- Canada's economy strengthened in the third quarter, increasing chances for a sustained expansion.
- Rank Group said it will not be joining as a partner for the struggling Trump's Castle resort in Atlantic City.
- Elektrowatt plans to spin off its electric power business, forming a new entity with $1.55 billion market capitalization.
- The U.S. and Britain will resume talks on a new "open skies" deal this week in London, seeking to narrow differences on several issues including access to London's crowded Heathrow Airport.
- Trust-preferred securities, a new form of preferred stock issued by banks and insurance companies, is increasing the trouble bonds are having in competing with stocks.
- Ronald Perelman's Revlon Inc is still looking good with its long-lasting ColorStay makeup, but the company's bonds and shares have been fading.
